entries.text: Addition from the coordinator, fold it into your plan: Codex's workspace-write sandbox blocks writes to .git (git commit fails with 'Unable to create .git/index.lock: Operation not permitted'). So in CI the common pattern is: codex exec edits files, then a later workflow step commits. That commit has no 'git commit' action in any session. Support it: a commit with no matching commit action gets the session(s) in that worktree whose last activity ended before the commit time and after the previous commit's time, matched as 'session' (a third match kind, shown in the viewer like the others), whole session segment since the previous commit. Keep sha/time matches preferred. Cover it with a test, and document it in docs/production.md (CI section). Also: the <path> commits are being re-recorded right now; wait until 'git -C <path> log --oneline' shows the wordfreq commits before step 7.
That works. Now I need to hook this up and test the full push flow end-to-end.
The CI pattern works on real data: matched `by session`, and one output clipped. Now the hook and `--push` end to end, through a real `git push` to a bare origin.

The ledgerCli header and production docs both look fine as-is. For commits, I'm planning to start with fixing Codex command quoting so it exactly matches what Codex displays, scoping that change to rollout.ts and deciding whether to defer the shellJoin test to a separate commit.

For the ledger fix I need to find where Codex's shell wrapper detects git commits, which means working with just part of ledger.ts. I'll construct intermediate versions by taking the HEAD content and applying selected changes in Python, then staging them with git hash-object and update-index — a clean way to build partial patches for commits.

I'm now laying out the full commit sequence: rollout.ts plus its shlex test, the ledger commit-detection fix with matching test cases, and a larger feature commit for reading sessions from rollout files without the app-server, which touches several components including CodexRollouts, ThreadStore, and their associated test fakes.

I'm weighing whether app.ts's ThreadStoreLive fallback belongs in this commit too, but decide to defer the full app.ts wiring to the next commit since CodexRollouts isn't required by Ledger yet — keeping commit 3's app.ts untouched. The remaining work — Ledger.ts, domain logic, ActionView, the CLI, and docs — will form commit 4, possibly splitting docs into their own commit since they describe the feature changes separately.

I'm still considering whether each intermediate commit can pass typecheck and tests on its own — checking that CodexRollouts.test's fixtures and ThreadStore.empty usage hold up, and that the new shellJoin export covers the shlex test. To actually verify this, I'm thinking I could spin up a git worktree for each commit and run the test suite there with a symlinked node_modules.

I'll do that verification pass at the end for each commit instead of blocking on it now. Also need to relocate the shlex test out of rolloutThread.test.ts and into rollout.test.ts.



Docs and checks are done. Now I'll commit changes one concern at a time using hash-object and update-index, starting with moving the shlex test into rollout.test.ts.

cd . && export PATH=$PWD/node_modules/.bin:$PATH && git diff --stat src/core/rollout.ts src/core/rollout.test.ts && git add src/core/rollout.ts src/core/rollout.test.ts && git -c user.email=<private> commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
fix(codex): quote rollout commands exactly as Codex shows them

Commands recovered from rollout files are joined from argv. Codex joins them
with Rust shlex: words are cut into bare, single- and double-quoted chunks,
and `^` always starts its own chunk. Matching it makes recovered commands
identical to what `codex app-server` reports (checked on 2,461 commands).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -1
